answer.text: Equity + debt in specified ratio (aggressive, conservative, balanced)

explanation.text: The Logic: A Hybrid Mutual Fund combines equity and debt within a single scheme in specified allocation bands. Standard sub-categories include aggressive hybrid (predominantly equity), conservative hybrid (predominantly debt), and balanced hybrid (roughly equal split), with the precise band defined by SEBI's MF categorisation framework. The Trap: A fund holding only bonds is a debt fund; only gold is a gold/commodity fund; only tax-saving (ELSS) is an equity-linked savings scheme. None of these qualify as hybrid schemes. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook discusses mutual fund access and broad classification by investment universe (equity, fixed income, money market, gold, international) but does not present the aggressive/conservative/balanced hybrid sub-categories with their allocation ratios on the pages checked. The hybrid taxonomy above reflects general industry/regulatory mutual fund classification.
